key_insight: The paper introduces an automated way to estimate floating-point rounding error inside finite element kernels as they run, enabling detection of hidden numerical instability.
engineering_relevance: This helps engineers build more reliable FEM solvers, especially for ill-conditioned problems, reduced-precision workflows, and debugging compiled kernel code.
method: Wrap kernel arithmetic in a custom type that tracks both value and running forward error.
Integrate Running Error Analysis (REA) into the FEniCS Form Compiler (FFCx) via a C++ backend.
Compute error estimates concurrently with kernel values during assembly.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two demonstrations—catastrophic cancellation in Neo-Hooke assembly and a near-degenerate Laplace mesh case—and states the implementation typically adds only 2-4x runtime overhead.
watch_item: The approach adds nontrivial runtime overhead and depends on compiler/backend integration, so deployment cost and kernel compatibility need care.
paper_title: Running error bounds in finite element kernels
